Title: Sacrorum conciliorum nova et amplissima collectio, in qua praeter ea quae Phil. Labbeus et Gabr. Cossartius et novissime Nicolaus Coleti in lucem edidere ... quae Joannes Dominicus Mansi archiepiscopus Lucensis evulgavit. Tomus trigesimus primus
Creator: Giovanni Domenico Mansi (ed.), after Philippe Labbe, Gabriel Cossart and Nicolas Coleti; the acts of the councils of Basel, Ferrara and Florence
Publisher: Facsimile reproduction (anastatic, 250 copies) printed by C. Reinecke, Berlin, for H. Welter, Paris and Leipzig, 1906, of the Venice edition of Zatta (the host catalogues it as 1798)
Publication Date: 1906
Rights: Public Domain
Rights basis: the facsimile's title page reads '1906' (file lines 139 and 134 of the OCR: '1906' and 'H. WELTER'); the underlying edition is of the eighteenth century; host record: date 1798, volume 31, no rights field.
Language: lat (Latin, with the Greek of the acts in parallel columns, mostly garbled in the OCR; see the content note)
Source: Internet Archive item sacrorumconcilio0031jonn (archive.org/details/sacrorumconcilio0031jonn), full-text file sacrorumconcilio0031jonn_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the Library thread, October 2026.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the Library thread; the OCR text follows it unchanged. Nothing was stripped, normalised, corrected, re-spaced or retyped (the long s glyph occurs 0 times and was left as found). The OCR text that follows is 3192025 bytes, 3153316 characters and 104831 lines. OCR quality sampled at the title pages and at about 5%, 50% and 95% of the file (lines 5254, 52428 and 99602): Latin readable with long s as f; Greek columns badly garbled (Greek letters rendered as Latin and punctuation); the Latin of the acts is the usable witness.
Content note: Mansi tomus 31. The file's own index heads 'Florentinum oecumenicum concilium' with the acts of Ferrara and Florence in Latin and Greek (Bessarion's oration, the sessions on purgatory, the procession of the Holy Spirit, the azymes and the primacy) and the 'Definitio synodi Florentinae', which is the decree Laetentur caeli (the OCR prints its opening 'Letentur coeli' near file lines 73472 and 97371). The volume also holds the later acts of the Council of Basel and the Council of Bourges. Latin runs with the long s read as f; the Greek of the parallel columns is garbled where it appears.
